recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead, an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No "@", no leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no "@" anywhere, no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

variables) and the native shell (`ShellTheme`). The design system itself lives
in the Figma file "JusPrin v2" and is mirrored, value for value, in a Claude
artifact. On 2026-10-19 Kenneth ruled that the design system is the source of
truth: where the token file disagrees with it, change the token file. This
document lists every known disagreement and what to do about each.

- Figma file "JusPrin v2", key `jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH`, Design System page

  components hold control sizes.

**What I checked**

**What's missing or unclear**

Those are the tokens in `design-tokens.json` that every screen reads. My guess is the sync hasn't started: its handoff is still untracked and I found no token-sync branch or worktree. I haven't confirmed that with whoever owns it. The token-sync handoff also has its own open questions for you, such as what to do with colours that exist only in the code. So I need you to decide: do the sync here first, or wait for another session to do it.

Two things to know about what's in the artifact:

1	# Handoff: bring the code's design tokens in line with the design system
2	
3	JusPrin's UI sizes and colours live in one token file,
4	`resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`, which feeds the Agent pages (CSS
5	variables) and the native shell (`ShellTheme`). The design system itself lives
6	in the Figma file "JusPrin v2" and is mirrored, value for value, in a Claude
7	artifact. On 2026-10-19 Kenneth ruled that the design system is the source of
8	truth: where the token file disagrees with it, change the token file. This
9	document lists every known disagreement and what to do about each.
10	
11	## Sources of truth
12	
13	- Figma file "JusPrin v2", key `jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH`, Design System page
14	  `9:153`. Variables hold colours, spacing, radius, elevation and text styles;
15	  components hold control sizes.
16	- The Design System artifact, https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL.
17	  Its `tokens.json` was generated from Figma's variables and matched them
18	  exactly at the last sync (2026-10-13). A local copy is at
19	  `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/published/ds/project/tokens.json`.
20	- Component sizes are not variables in Figma; they are the sizes of the
21	  components themselves. The table below was read from the local copy of the
22	  Design System page, `figma-mirror/figma/spec3/9-153.txt`. Note: the Composer
23	  component was rebuilt in Figma after that read and the new read is
24	  incomplete, so treat the Composer's numbers there as stale.
25	
26	## Differences found
27	
28	### Colours
29	
30	Light-mode values match. Three dark-mode status colours differ:
31	
32	| Token | Design system (dark) | Code (dark) |
33	|---|---|---|
34	| success | `#4CAF82` | `#58B894` (`primitive.successDark`) |
35	| danger | `#E07080` | `#F07A8E` |
36	| warning | `#E8B84A` | `#E9B960` |
37	
38	These colours exist only in the code, with no design-system counterpart:
39	`action.secondary`, `secondaryHover`, `secondaryPressed`, `secondaryText`,
40	`secondaryBorder`, `action.danger`, `dangerText`, `dangerBorder`,
41	`overlayScrim`, `statusSuccessOnAction`, `textOnAction`. Ask Kenneth whether
42	each should be added to Figma (then the artifact) or replaced by an existing
43	design-system colour. Do not delete them on your own.
44	
45	### Radius
46	
47	| Design system | Value | Code | Value |
48	|---|---|---|---|
49	| radius-small | 4 | `dimension.radius.standard` | 4 |
50	| radius-medium | 8 | `compact`, `container` | 8, 8 |
51	| radius-large | 12 | `window` | 12 |
52	| radius-chip | 4 | (no token; `component.chip.radius` 4) | 4 |
53	| radius-full | 10 | `pill` | 9999 |
54	
55	Values agree except `full` (10) vs `pill` (9999). Names differ throughout.
56	Decide with Kenneth whether to rename the code tokens to the design-system
57	names (touches every consumer and guard test) or keep the code names and only
58	fix the values. Renaming is cleaner but a larger diff.
59	
60	### Spacing, elevation, text styles
61	
62	Same in both. Nothing to do.
63	
64	### Control sizes (Figma component vs code token)
65	
66	| Component | Figma | Code token | Code value | Action |
67	|---|---|---|---|---|
68	| Button/Icon | 32x32, radius 4 | `component.button.icon` | 26x26 | change to 32 |
69	| Button/Primary | 34 high, padding 8/16, radius 8 | `button.primary` | padding 8/16, radius 8 | same; check the rendered height is 34 |
70	| Button/Secondary | 32 high, padding 6/12, radius 4 | `button.secondary` | padding 6/12 | same; check height 32 |
71	| Button/Link | 26 high, padding 0/4 | none found | | find what the code uses |
72	| Menu/Row | 36 high, full width, padding 8/12, gap 8, no radius | `menuRow` | 32 high, radius 4, side inset 4 | change, but see the warning below |

# Handoff: bring the code's design tokens in line with the design system

JusPrin's UI sizes and colours live in one token file,
`resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`, which feeds the Agent pages (CSS
variables) and the native shell (`ShellTheme`). The design system itself lives
in the Figma file "JusPrin v2" and is mirrored, value for value, in a Claude
artifact. On 2026-10-19 Kenneth ruled that the design system is the source of
truth: where the token file disagrees with it, change the token file. This
document lists every known disagreement and what to do about each.

## Sources of truth

- Figma file "JusPrin v2", key `jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH`, Design System page
  `9:153`. Variables hold colours, spacing, radius, elevation and text styles;
  components hold control sizes.
- The Design System artifact, https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL.
  Its `tokens.json` was generated from Figma's variables and matched them
  exactly at the last sync (2026-10-13). A local copy is at
  `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/published/ds/project/tokens.json`.
- Component sizes are not variables in Figma; they are the sizes of the
  components themselves. The table below was read from the local copy of the
  Design System page, `figma-mirror/figma/spec3/9-153.txt`. Note: the Composer
  component was rebuilt in Figma after that read and the new read is
  incomplete, so treat the Composer's numbers there as stale.

## Differences found

### Colours

Light-mode values match. Three dark-mode status colours differ:

| Token | Design system (dark) | Code (dark) |
|---|---|---|
| success | `#4CAF82` | `#58B894` (`primitive.successDark`) |
| danger | `#E07080` | `#F07A8E` |
| warning | `#E8B84A` | `#E9B960` |

These colours exist only in the code, with no design-system counterpart:
`action.secondary`, `secondaryHover`, `secondaryPressed`, `secondaryText`,
`secondaryBorder`, `action.danger`, `dangerText`, `dangerBorder`,
`overlayScrim`, `statusSuccessOnAction`, `textOnAction`. Ask Kenneth whether
each should be added to Figma (then the artifact) or replaced by an existing
design-system colour. Do not delete them on your own.

### Radius

| Design system | Value | Code | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| radius-small | 4 | `dimension.radius.standard` | 4 |
| radius-medium | 8 | `compact`, `container` | 8, 8 |
| radius-large | 12 | `window` | 12 |
| radius-chip | 4 | (no token; `component.chip.radius` 4) | 4 |
| radius-full | 10 | `pill` | 9999 |

Values agree except `full` (10) vs `pill` (9999). Names differ throughout.
Decide with Kenneth whether to rename the code tokens to the design-system
names (touches every consumer and guard test) or keep the code names and only
fix the values. Renaming is cleaner but a larger diff.

### Spacing, elevation, text styles

Same in both. Nothing to do.

### Control sizes (Figma component vs code token)

| Component | Figma | Code token | Code value | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Button/Icon | 32x32, radius 4 | `component.button.icon` | 26x26 | change to 32 |
| Button/Primary | 34 high, padding 8/16, radius 8 | `button.primary` | padding 8/16, radius 8 | same; check the rendered height is 34 |
| Button/Secondary | 32 high, padding 6/12, radius 4 | `button.secondary` | padding 6/12 | same; check height 32 |
| Button/Link | 26 high, padding 0/4 | none found | | find what the code uses |
| Menu/Row | 36 high, full width, padding 8/12, gap 8, no radius | `menuRow` | 32 high, radius 4, side inset 4 | change, but see the warning below |
| Menu/Popover | 280 wide, padding 8 top/bottom, row gap 2, radius 8 | `popover` | padding 4, gap 0, radius 8 | change, but see the warning below |
| Chip/Printer+Spool | 28 high, radius 4 | `chip` | 26 high | change, but see the warning below |
| Chat/Reply Choice | 28 high, padding 0/12 | `replyChip` | 28, 12 | same |
| Field/Number, Select, Form Row | 26 high, radius 4 | `field`, `select`, `formRow` | 26 | same |
| Field/Search | 38 high, padding 8/10 | not checked | | compare |
| Segmented Control | 30 high, padding 2, radius 4 | not checked | | compare |
| Tooltip | 24 high, padding 4/8, radius 4 | not checked | | compare |
| Swatch | 24, radius 4 | `swatch` | 24, 4 | same |
| Status Dot | 8 | `statusDot` | 8 | same |
| Progress | 4 high | `progress` | 4 | same |
| Tool Panel | padding 12, gap 8, radius 8 | `toolPanel` | padding 12 | same |
| Sheet | padding 24, gap 16, radius 12 | not checked | | compare |

Finish the "not checked" rows before changing anything, so Kenneth sees the
whole list at once.

## Warning: Kenneth rejected the Figma header menu sizes once before

On 2026-09-07 Kenneth reverted the header printer/filament chip and its menu
from Figma's sizes back to the current ones (commit "Revert my header menu
restyling: it looked worse and I could not explain why", on `jusprin-newui`).
The values he kept then: chip 26 high, menu rows 32 high with radius 4 and a
4 px side inset, popover padding 4 with no gap between rows. Figma's values
(chip 28, rows 36 full width, padding 8, gap 2) are exactly what he rejected.

His 2026-10-19 ruling says the design system wins, but it was made about the
Agent chat composer, not with that revert in front of him. Before changing the
chip, Menu/Row or Menu/Popover tokens, show Kenneth both versions side by side
(a picture of the header menu at each size) and ask which one he wants. If he
keeps the code's values, the fix goes the other way: change Figma, then
re-sync the artifact.

## How to do it

1. Work in a new worktree off `jusprin-newui`. Do not use another session's
   worktree.
2. Read `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` ("Writing UI code") and the
   guard tests: `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` (native) and
   `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.test.ts` (Agent pages).
3. For each change: update the token, update the guard test so it expects the
   new value, and prove the guard fails first (set the old value back, see it
   fail, restore from a saved copy, never with `git checkout`).
4. Rebuild the Agent page bundles and the app, and check every screen that
   uses a changed token in light and dark: the header chip and its menu, the
   Agent chat (composer, reply chips, tool activity), Home, the printer
   dialog, and the settings forms. Capture pictures for Kenneth.
5. Read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` before touching any file
   outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`.
6. Commit only when Kenneth asks.

## Related work

The composer redesign (`handoff-composer-redesign.md`, worktree
`JusPrin-worktrees/composer-redesign`) needs the new Button/Icon, Menu/Row and
Menu/Popover sizes. It adds one new token group, `component.composer`
(padding 8, gap 4, inputPadding 4, maxLines 8), which is not yet in Figma.
Coordinate so the two changes do not edit the same lines of the token file at
the same time.

Leave this file untracked. Do not commit it or add it to any ignore file.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

159:## Writing UI code
160-
161-Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
162-exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from Figma and from
163-the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
164-only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.
165-
166-1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
167-   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
168-   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
169-   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
170-   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
171-   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
172-   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
173-   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
174-   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
175-2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
176-   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
177-   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
178-   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
179-   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
180-   value that exists in Figma but not in the roles or scales is a design
181-   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
182-3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
183-   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
184-   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
185-4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
186-   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
187-   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
188-5. **Read the code on `jusprin-newui`, not old commit messages or Figma,
189-   when they disagree.** The header's chip and menu dimensions were once
190-   changed to match Figma and reverted because they looked worse; the
191-   token file records what stayed.
192-6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
193-   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
194-   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
195-   not that the result looks right.
196-7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
197-   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
198-   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
199-   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.
200-
201-## Runtime application in the native app
202-
203-The token file is applied to the running application in three layers. All
204-three read `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; none of them carries a
205-color literal of its own, and the whole layer touches OrcaSlicer code in only
206-three small, additive seams plus one attachment point.
207-
208-1. **Fork-owned surfaces** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/*`, the React Agent
209-   page) resolve every style through the token file, not only color.
210-   - Native: `ShellTheme` exposes `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for
211-     the radius and spacing scales and the per-component sizes, `font(role)`
212-     for the type roles above. It is loaded once, by `Brand/BrandPalette.cpp`, and passed
213-     by reference into every shell widget. Widgets that paint themselves read
214-     it directly; a stock `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button`
215-     is dressed through the three functions in `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, so no
216-     fork-owned C++ file names an OrcaSlicer font preset or writes a radius as
217-     a number. `tests/jusprin/test_shell_theme.cpp` checks the parse and the
218-     fonts.
219-   - Web: `AgentUI/src/tokens.ts` writes the semantic colors as

content.content:
description: Have the app draw its own widgets into a PNG for appearance evidence; behavioural assertions miss visual defects entirely, and screen capture is often unavailable.
  type: feedback

For fork-owned wx controls, split painting from the paint event —
`paint(wxPaintEvent&)` builds the DC and delegates to
`draw(wxDC&, wxGraphicsContext&, wxSize)` — then add `snapshot()` that draws into
a `wxMemoryDC` over a `wxBitmap`. The shell harness writes those PNGs each run
(honour an env var like `JUSPRIN_ARTIFACT_DIR`; the harness deletes its temp data
dir at exit, so artifacts written there vanish before you can look).

Note `wxGraphicsContext::Create` has no generic `wxDC` overload — each caller
must build the context for its own concrete DC and pass it in.

**Why:** on the printer/spool chip slice, 267 green harness checks coexisted with
two real rendering defects, both found only by opening the image: a long-name
snapshot byte-identical to the normal one (the capture helper called `refresh()`
first, which re-read the store and undid the test's label — so the width
assertion compared a value to itself), and an inline detail overrunning the
trailing chevron under width pressure (measured width was correct; the overlap
was a painting error). Screen-control access was denied and `screencapture`
could not see the window, so in-app rendering was the only route.

**How to apply:** assert on raw pixel buffers (`wxImage::GetData` + `memcmp`) —
"light differs from dark", "long name differs from normal" — so a silently
reverted label fails instead of passing. Then still *open the image*; the
assertions prove difference, not correctness. See
[[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[jusprin-chip-orca-seams]].
description: "How to capture the fork's wx popup menus on macOS for a pixel comparison against Windows captures, and why Windows text renders ~9% larger than the tokens intend."
  type: project

To compare Windows screenshots against macOS, run the same
`shell_integration_harness` fixture on both and capture each popup by window id.

**Why:** `screencapture` and any ScreenCaptureKit path fail from the Bash tool
("could not create image from display") — the Screen Recording grant belongs to a
process I cannot reach. The computer-use `app_screenshot` tool is the only route,
and it accepts a **raw CGWindowID**, not just ids from `app_list_windows`. Popups
never appear in `app_list_windows`, so enumerate them yourself.

**How to apply:**
- Build a tiny Swift lister (`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionOnScreenOnly)`
  filtered by pid). The fork's `HeaderMenu` popups show up at `layer=101`; the main
  window is `layer=0`. Feed that id to `app_screenshot` for native-resolution pixels.
- Drive clicks with a Swift `CGEvent` helper at **global** coords
  (window origin + local). The app need not be frontmost.
- Only the **chip halves** respond to synthetic clicks. The header's overflow "…",
  the split-button chevron, and the Home back button do not — that is a limitation
  of the automation, **not** an application bug. Use the harness's own
  `--header-visual` / `--review-visual` modes for those screens instead.
- While a popup is open, the next click anywhere only dismisses it. Budget two
  clicks. Escape does not close them.
- Put the window on the **Acer H226HQL** (1920x1080, non-Retina): the harness's
  1200x800 window is then 1:1 with a Windows capture at 100% scaling, so popup
  sizes compare directly. On the built-in Retina display they would not.

**Windows text is ~9% LARGER than macOS, not smaller.** `Label::sysFont`
(`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/Label.cpp:19`) multiplies the point size by 4/5 off Apple
to offset Windows' 96 DPI against macOS' 72 — but 96/72 x 4/5 = 1.067, so it
under-corrects. Measured on the chip: glyph height 12 px Windows vs 11 px macOS.
Consequence: fixed-width popups ellipsize *more* on Windows. Do not assume the 4/5
factor makes Windows text smaller. Mono text goes the other way (Courier New is
narrower than Menlo), so the chip itself comes out 346 px on Windows vs 353 on Mac.

See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[windows-gui-test-vm-gcp]],
[[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
  type: feedback

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

content.text:
I've finished comparing the code's design tokens (the size and colour values in `design-tokens.json`) with Figma. Most of the differences I can just fix, since you ruled that Figma wins. Four need your decision before I change anything, and the header menu is the biggest. Nothing has been changed yet.

**The header menu.** The two pictures above show the printer menu at both sets of sizes. The app drew them itself, because macOS blocks screen capture from here. A is today's sizes, the ones you kept when you reverted the Figma restyle on 2026-09-07. B is Figma's: chip 28, rows 36 at full width, padding 8, a 2 px gap between rows. Three things to know about B:
- The same menu size values also set the Home printer card's menu and the print-issue list.
- Full-width rows paint over the popover's 1 px border. You can see the breaks in the border in B. To match Figma exactly, the rows would sit 1 px in from the edge.
- The Agent chat's own menus don't use these values at all today; they have their sizes typed into the CSS. I'd switch them to the shared values whichever size you pick, so the composer's + menu matches the header.

**What I'll fix unless you object.** Each of these follows your "Figma wins" ruling:
- **Dark status colours** move to Figma's: success `#4CAF82`, danger `#E07080`, warning `#E8B84A`. The danger text and border on dark buttons repeat the old danger colour by hand, so they change with it. The three separate dark status entries in the token file have no users and get deleted.
- **Buttons.** The Agent page's general-purpose primary button renders 38 high and its secondary 34. Home's primary renders 36. Figma has 34 and 32. I'd bring them in line using the button settings the Agent dialogs already use, which hit 34 and 32 exactly.
- **Text-only link buttons.** On the Agent setup page and the printer panel headers they render 16 to 20 high with no padding, and the setup page's uses the larger 14 px bold font. Figma has 26 high, 4 px side padding, 12 px bold. I'd add a link-button token and use it everywhere.
- **The provider switch on the Agent setup page.** It's the only segmented control, and it renders 34 high with radius 8 and 14 px text. Figma has 30 high, radius 4, 12 px segments. I'd add a token for it.
- **The one custom tooltip** (the revert button's tooltip in the Agent chat) changes to Figma's dark ink tooltip. The other tooltips are the operating system's own and stay as they are.
- **Home's printer dialog** spaces its contents with one-off margins. I'd change it to Figma's 24 padding and 16 gap, which the Agent dialog already uses.
- **The design-system guide** (`design-system.md`) says that when code and Figma disagree, the code wins. Your ruling reverses that, so I'll rewrite that rule.
- **Already the same:** spacing, shadows, text styles, light-mode colours, the reply chip, fields, selects, swatches, status dots and progress bars. Figma's search field doesn't exist in the code yet.

**Why the icon button needs a decision.** A guard test in `test_brand_tokens.cpp:456` requires a text field, a select and an icon button to be the same height, so a field and its reset button line up in a form row. Figma's fields are 26 and its icon button is 32. Moving the icon button to 32 breaks that rule. It also enlarges the header's pane toggles, the canvas tool strip, the reset buttons in tool panels, the print-issue bubble, Home's card menu button and the Agent's Send button.

| `border.subtle` | `#E8DFEB` | `#4B3E57` | Dividers and quiet structure |
| `border.strong` | `#6F4F84` | `#7D6A8D` | Focus and essential boundaries |
| `action.primary` | `#3A2D64` | `#CE84B7` | Decisive primary action |
| `action.primary.hover` | `#4B3A77` | `#D99AC5` | Pointer hover |
| `action.primary.pressed` | `#2B214F` | `#B76CA0` | Pressed or active state |

The JSON token file is authoritative and contains the complete action, status, selected-surface, disabled, text, and component values.

## Typography

Product UI uses fonts already shipped by OrcaSlicer:

- HarmonyOS Sans SC Regular for body and controls.
- HarmonyOS Sans SC Bold for hierarchy and actions.
- NanumGothic for Korean and Sarabun for Thai where the existing application requires them.
- The system GUI font as fallback.
- The system monospace font only for code: API keys, file paths, commands, config text, and IDs such as hashes. Never for names, words, or measurements.

HarmonyOS Sans SC draws every digit at the same width, so times, percentages,
and other values that change in place do not shift in the UI face; they do
not need the monospace one. The native shell has no monospace text.

Never require Menlo or another platform-specific face. The broader marketing brand kit used Avenir Next for display and marketing; that is not the cross-platform product UI requirement.

| Role | Size/line height in DIP | Weight |
|---|---:|---|
| Page title | 24/30 | Bold |
| Section | 18/24 | Bold |
| Body and control | 14/20 | Regular |
| Body bold | 14/20 | Bold |
| Body small | 13/18 | Regular |
| Body small bold | 13/18 | Bold |
| Label | 12/16 | Regular |
| Label bold | 12/16 | Bold |
| Dense metadata | 10/14 | Regular |
| Dense metadata bold | 10/14 | Bold |
| Code (system monospace) | 12/16 | Regular |

The bold pairs exist for emphasis inside a run of the same size (a primary
action beside secondary ones, the current row of a menu, a chip's name beside
its detail). Code is a single role, `typography.code`, whatever size the
text around it is.

## Layout and geometry

Design for a dense, native, high-DPI desktop application on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Use device-independent pixels (DIP), not physical pixels. Verify 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling.

- Spacing scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, and 48 DIP.
- Standard control radius: 4 DIP, matching OrcaSlicer's own controls.
- Compact or branded action radius: 8 DIP.
- Container radius: 8 DIP, for grouped panels and cards, matching OrcaSlicer's `StaticBox` default.
- Window action and large-dialog radius: 12 DIP.
- Capsule radius: `pill`, for status chips and progress tracks whose shape is
  the full height. Menu rows sit inset 4 DIP inside the popover and carry the
  standard radius, so a hovered row reads as a control inside the panel
  rather than a stripe across it.
- Reserve 16–24 DIP radii for onboarding and marketing, not the main application shell.

Avoid web-only assumptions such as oversized controls, blur-heavy or glass surfaces, fixed physical pixels, and platform-specific fonts.

## Components and states

Use the existing native component density and Lucide `v1.47.0` SVG artwork for generic functional icons. Pin the artwork in `resources/jusprin/ui/icons` and use the same SVG geometry in Figma, the React pages, and the native shell; a package or plugin alone is not the cross-surface source of truth. Keep the JusPrin mark and product-specific symbols custom. Functional clarity comes before logo-derived decoration.

- Functional icons: Lucide artwork at 16, 20, or 24 DIP, colored through the surrounding semantic token, with PNG fallback when the platform path requires it. Do not create a separate UI component for each glyph.
- Setup card fact glyphs: 14 DIP from `component.setupCard.iconSize`, the one size below the icon scale. The clock, material, plate, warning, and info glyphs sit inside a row of Label or Metadata text, 14 to 16 DIP tall, and a 16 DIP glyph makes that row taller than its text. The card's disclosure chevron is an ordinary 16 DIP icon. Do not use this size on another surface; it is not a step of the icon scale.
- Shared progress track: 4 DIP from `component.progress.height`; PrinterCard and Agent activity use this role rather than owning separate track heights.
- Orbit motif: progress, connection, or active workflow; verify stroke clarity at output size.
- Directional accent: at most one diagonal for momentum; avoid decorative competing angles.
- Compact button: 8×3 DIP padding, 8 DIP radius, dense metadata text.
- Window button: minimum 58×24 DIP, 12 DIP radius, 12 DIP text.
- Choice control: minimum 100×32 DIP, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
- Parameter control: 120×26 DIP, 4 DIP radius, 14 DIP text.
- Icon button: 26×26 DIP, 16 DIP icon, 4 DIP radius.
- Expanded button: at least 32 DIP high, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
- Plates / Project pane: 200 DIP wide on `surface.subtle`, a 12 DIP band above a 36 DIP tab strip (the active tab is Label Bold with a 2 DIP `action.primary` rule; the other is Label in `text.secondary`). Plate rows are 32 DIP, object rows 36 DIP, both on `surface.canvas` blocks with the standard radius and a 2 DIP gap; a folded plate adds a 20 DIP Metadata summary line indented 32 DIP. Every number is under `component.leftPane`, taken from the Figma frames on the Plates & Project Pane page.
- Agent-pane divider: transparent 8 DIP pointer target with a centered 2 DIP line; the line changes from subtle to strong on hover and to the primary action color while dragging.
- Agent-pane width: minimum 320 DIP; its maximum follows the window width while preserving at least 320 DIP for the workspace.
- Printer setup, connecting, printer settings, and filament settings help use the same temporary conversation layer over the originating workspace. The underlying Home, Prepare, or Preview screen stays selected and constructed so Back returns to it. The conversation keeps the centered content width from `component.printerSetup.contentWidth` and the existing task header controls; manual settings remain available from that header. The saved project Agent pane remains a separate persistent conversation.
- Agent-pane collapse: a 26 DIP icon button in the header, left of the overflow button, whose glyph fills its right-hand column while the pane is open and empties it while the pane is closed. Double-clicking the divider closes the pane. Dragging it does not: a drag only sizes the pane and stops at its 320 DIP minimum, so aiming for a narrow pane never takes the conversation off the screen. There is no keyboard shortcut, no animation, and no automatic reopening; the pane is hidden, never destroyed, so its conversation survives. Reopening restores the width it last held.

Every interactive component must define normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focused, success, warning, and error states where relevant. Status must combine color with an icon and plain-language label.

## Accessibility

- Normal text requires at least 4.5:1 contrast; 3:1 is allowed only for large text.
- Essential control boundaries and state indicators require 3:1.
- Keyboard focus uses a visible 2 DIP ring and may not rely on a fill-color change alone.
- Orbit on White measures 12.07:1 in the source design system.
- Bloom on Ink measures 6.62:1.
- Light secondary text measures 6.89:1 on White.
- Dark secondary text measures 10.95:1 on Ink.

The clock, material, plate, warning, and info glyphs sit inside a row of Label or Metadata text, 14 to 16 DIP tall, and a 16 DIP glyph makes that row taller than its text. The card's disclosure chevron is an ordinary 16 DIP icon. Do not use this size on another surface; it is not a step of the icon scale.

- Orbit motif: progress, connection, or active workflow; verify stroke clarity at output size.

- Window button: minimum 58×24 DIP, 12 DIP radius, 12 DIP text.
- Choice control: minimum 100×32 DIP, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
- Parameter control: 120×26 DIP, 4 DIP radius, 14 DIP text.

- Expanded button: at least 32 DIP high, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.

The conversation keeps the centered content width from `component.printerSetup.contentWidth` and the existing task header controls; manual settings remain available from that header. Dragging it does not: a drag only sizes the pane and stops at its 320 DIP minimum, so aiming for a narrow pane never takes the conversation off the screen. - Normal text requires at least 4.5:1 contrast; 3:1 is allowed only for large text.
- Essential control boundaries and state indicators require 3:1.
- Keyboard focus uses a visible 2 DIP ring and may not rely on a fill-color change alone.
- Orbit on White measures 12.07:1 in the source design system.
- Bloom on Ink measures 6.62:1.
- Light secondary text measures 6.89:1 on White.
- Dark secondary text measures 10.95:1 on Ink.

description: "computer_batch save_to_disk produced no files (2026-09-23); to get screenshot files for a report, replay the observed host state into the built Agent/Home page under Playwright, which saves PNGs; plus the window-overlap trap when another session runs the harness."
  type: project
---

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

### State matrices

`src/visual/` holds one state input per state on the Figma page **Agent UI ·
States & Components**: runtime and header states, chat
list, composer, messages, manufacturing history, the earlier-chat notice, and
the printer chat. Each is rendered by the production components, or by the
real `App` against a scripted host, so a state is covered only if real inputs
can produce it. `npm test` asserts every one renders; with an output path the
same test writes a review page of all of them at the 429 and 320 DIP dock
widths in both appearances:

```bash
PREVIEW_OUT=/tmp/agent-ui-states.html npx vitest run AgentUiStateMatrix
```

Open the page with `?show=<case>,<case>&mode=dark&dock=320` to narrow it to
the states being compared with a Figma node. The page proves rendering only;
look at the running app as well (`tests/shell`'s capture modes write PNGs of
the real WebView).

`tokens.ts` imports `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json` at build time
and writes it onto the root element as custom properties: `--<group>-<name>`
for the semantic colors of the appearance the host reports, and, once at

complete `font` shorthand of each type role and `--font-code` for the one
monospace role, used only for code, keys, paths and IDs. `styles.css` may use only those variables for

   text. Only `overlay.scrim` and `status.successOnAction` stay code-only

   large 12, chip 4, full 10 (pill 9999 is gone).

composer; these answers confirm it for the shared tokens too.

the strength of the old memory or the 2026-09-07 commit.

entries.name: mcp__ccd_session__start_session
entries.description:
Start a separate Claude Code session for a task while you stay with the user (when: see "Starting other sessions"). `initiation` says who wants it: "user_asked" starts it now and returns its id; "offer" is for a task the user named in their latest message (new work here, or "suggest / split off / make a task or session for X"): called with a title alone, it shows a "New session" / "Do it here" card and WAITS for their answer, so it must be the only call in that message (no update_plan, no other tool); the result then tells you to carry on here, or to send the brief with proposal_id so the session starts; "own_initiative" is for work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up (when your reply calls work a follow-up or a separate PR, propose it here rather than only saying so); the user sees a card and nothing runs until they start it, by clicking it or by telling you (then call this again with just proposal_id).
"user_asked" and "own_initiative" both need a `prompt` — the brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like — and the call is refused without it; `background` does not stand in for it. Only an "offer" is a title alone.
context: "fork" = this whole conversation + your `prompt`. "fresh" (default) = your `prompt` + `background` only, so `background` is required too, at least 80 characters.
Checkout here ("fresh" only): use_worktree false = shares this checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session its branch and PR too: never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); true = its own worktree (the default when this session is in one).
Elsewhere ("fresh", user_asked only, when the user named the place): `cwd`, `target` "ssh" + `host`, `environment` or `preset`; list_start_targets lists the valid names.

initiation.description: "user_asked": the user asked in words for separate, parallel or background work, or told you to start this piece — it starts now. "offer": a task the user named in their latest message (new work for this session, or one they asked you to suggest, split off or make a session for) — the user is asked first and the call waits for their answer; send only title with it (the brief follows, with proposal_id, if they choose New session). "own_initiative": work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up; it waits as a proposal card until the user starts it; never for a task the user's message tells you to do. Required unless proposal_id is set.

proposal_id.description: Start a proposal the user told you to start, exactly as proposed: its task_id and nothing else (wake_when_done may accompany a local one). To change it, dismiss_task it and start a new session.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task. Shown on the row or card. Required unless proposal_id is set.

prompt.description: The brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like. Required for "user_asked" and "own_initiative" — the call is refused without it, and `background` does not stand in for it; an "offer" leaves it out (the card shows the user's own message) and you send it with proposal_id once they choose New session.

context.description: "fresh" (default) or "fork" — see the tool description. A "fork" from a worktree session gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip (commit first; uncommitted edits stay here); from a plain checkout it shares the folder.

background.description: Required with "fresh", besides `prompt`: at least 80 characters of overall goal, decisions and constraints so far, how this piece fits — for someone who has not seen this conversation. Ignored for "fork".

wake_when_done.description: Once this session (and any sibling still working) ends its turn, or fails to start (unless it waits at a prompt the user answers there, its folder was never opened in Claude Desktop, or the user started, stopped or archived it), and you are idle, the app continues you, whether or not this is set. true also continues you if this session never gets its task some other way, such as a brief that is not sent; default false; not with own_initiative; ignored with target "cloud", which never continues you.

name.description: Optional short handle for the session ([a-z0-9-], ≤24), e.g. "cli-cleanup". Linked sessions and plan steps refer to it by this name; derived from the title when omitted.

use_worktree.description: "fresh" only (rejected with "fork"). false = shares this session's checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session: its worktree, branch and PR, so never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); not accepted from a session set up to move from the user's checkout into a worktree with EnterWorktree (before or after it moves), one working in a worktree on an SSH host, or one whose worktree was given back. At another place named by `cwd`, `host` or `preset`, false = that folder as it is. true = its own git worktree. Omitted: the same folder when this session works in a plain folder and has never had a worktree (its own, a shared one, or one it will enter later); otherwise its own worktree. Omitted with `preset` or `host`, or with `cwd` from a session on an SSH host: the default set on that preset or SSH connection instead.

model.description: "fresh" only, optional: a cheaper model id for mechanical or read-only pieces (e.g. a Sonnet or Haiku id). Same family or cheaper than yours; anything higher is ignored. Omit to inherit yours.

target.description: "fresh" only. "local" (default) = where this session runs. "cloud" = run it as a cloud session (keeps going when this computer sleeps). Needs the repository on GitHub and a cloud environment — the app checks and tells the user if it cannot, and the task then stays as a card for them to start. model/effort/use_worktree/cwd/source_branch do not apply. Only when the user asks for the cloud. "ssh" = on the SSH connection named by host (or by a preset).

host.description: With target "ssh": the name of one of the user's saved SSH connections (as list_start_targets reports it) — never a raw hostname, user or key. The app connects as the user configured it and may ask them to sign in.

cwd.description: The folder the session works in, when it is not this project: an absolute (or ~/) path on the host it will run on — this computer, this session's host, or the SSH connection named by host (default there: the connection's folder). "fresh" only.

environment.description: With target "cloud": the name or id of one of the user's cloud environments (list_start_targets lists them); omitted = the default one.

repository.description: With target "cloud", only when the user named a repository other than this project's: "owner/name" on github.com, which the cloud session clones at its default branch. Take the exact owner/name from the user's words or a listing that shows it; if you are not sure of it, ask them. A bypass or auto permission mode may not carry over: the session then starts in the cloud's default mode. If the call is refused, do not run or propose the other repository's work in this project.

source_branch.description: The existing local branch the new worktree is cut from. Default in this project: this session's base branch (the one picked when it started, or the one its worktree was cut from). If the session has none and either it runs on an SSH host or its project folder is itself a git worktree or submodule, the folder's current commit. Otherwise, the repository's default branch, or the folder's current commit if that is unknown. Only for a session that gets its own worktree (use_worktree true, or the place's default); not with target "cloud".

branch_name.description: A short slug for the new worktree's branch (the app adds the user's branch prefix and a suffix). Only with a worktree.

preset.description: The name of one of the user's saved session presets on this computer: it names the place itself (a folder here or an SSH connection and folder — do not pass host or cwd with it) and brings model, effort and worktree defaults plus its saved environment variables; use_worktree/model/effort override those. Cloud and Remote Control presets are not available here.

effort.description: "fresh" only, optional: reasoning effort at or below yours. Omit to inherit.

permission_mode.description: Optional, local starts only: the permission mode it starts in — this session's own or a lower one (omit to inherit it). A higher mode, or one the app does not offer here, is refused; raising a session is set_session_permission_mode's card to show.

The token sync is done in its own worktree (`JusPrin-worktrees/design-token-sync`, branch `claude/design-token-sync`) and is not committed yet. The code's design tokens now match Figma under your four decisions. Every guard passes, and the pictures above show each changed screen in light and dark.

**What changed**
- **Header chip and menus** use Figma's sizes: chip 28, rows 36 at full width, popover padding 8 with a 2 px gap. The rows sit inside the popover's border, so the outline stays whole. My first capture showed rows painting over it, and I fixed that. Home's card menu, the print-issue list and the Agent chat menus now use the same values.
- **Icon buttons** are 32. A new 26 px compact token covers only the canvas tool strip and the reset buttons in form rows, because Figma uses 26 in exactly those two places. The guard now ties field height to the compact token.
- **Colours.** Dark-mode success, danger and warning are Figma's. Secondary and danger buttons use Figma's colours: no fill of their own, with a `border-subtle` or `status-danger` edge. The code-only button colours are gone; the scrim and success-on-action colours remain.
- **Radius names** are Figma's everywhere (small, medium, large, chip, full), in the native code, the CSS and the guard tests.
- **Link buttons, the setup page's provider switch, the revert tooltip and primary buttons** read new recipes: link 26 high, segmented control 30, tooltip 24, primary 34. Home's dialogs use Figma's Sheet spacing.
- **The design guide** (`design-system.md`) now says the design system wins when it and the code disagree.

**Tests.** Native guards: brand tokens and ShellTheme (344 assertions). Page tests: Agent 448, Home 61, and both pages typecheck. The full native harness passes 563 checks with 0 failures. The new guards fail when run against the old token file and the old stylesheet: five native guards and eight page guards.

**Not done or not checked yet**
- Not checked on Windows or Linux.
- The Agent chat header's own icon buttons are still 26 px, because their size is typed into the CSS rather than read from a token.
- Home's danger button is still 36 high. Figma has no danger button to match.
- The Agent page's Send button grew to 32 until the composer redesign replaces it.
- Figma doesn't have the scrim or success-on-action colours yet. I proposed a separate session for that, shown on the card above.

The composer work edits five of the same files. So the next step is to commit this sync and move the composer's uncommitted changes on top of it.
