coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Kenneth approved the model-menu search design and decided the narrow-width question. Please build both on claude/composer-redesign.

A. Narrow pane (Kenneth: drop "Thinking:" at narrow widths). Canvas board "composer-redesign · proposal", new state 11 "Narrow pane". When the full labels don't fit beside + and Send, the thinking picker first shows the level alone ("Medium" instead of "Thinking: Medium"). I measured it: at the 320 px minimum (296 px box) that alone is still 37 px too wide, so if it still doesn't fit, the model label is then cut with an ellipsis ("Claude…"). + (32) and Send keep their size. Keep the full text available to assistive tech (aria-label "Thinking: Medium") and as a tooltip. Use a container measurement or container query on the box rather than a fixed breakpoint, so it follows the actual label lengths.

B. Model menu search. Canvas board "model-menu-search · proposal" (Agent UI page, right of the composer proposal), marked approved:
1. When the model menu lists more than 12 models in total, it starts with a Field/Search ("Search models"), inset space-8 left and right, 4 px above the list, pinned while the list scrolls under it. With 12 or fewer models, no field (today's plain list).
2. The menu opens with focus in the field, so typing filters at once.
3. Filter: case-insensitive substring match on the model name or the provider name. Provider groups with no match drop out; the section titles stay for groups that have matches.
4. The first match is highlighted with the menu-row focus fill (surface-raised-hover). Enter picks it; Up and Down move between matches. The current model keeps its tick.
5. No match: a body-small text-secondary line "No models match “<query>”." in place of the rows, padded 8/12.
6. Escape clears the query; a second Escape closes the menu.
7. A section title may carry the provider's count: "OPENROUTER · 312 MODELS". Optional; only if the count is free to compute.
The README of the Composer card in the Design System artifact (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) has the same rules in prose.

Use the existing FieldSearch look from the token file (38 px high, radius-small, 1 px border-subtle, focused 2 px border-strong, search glyph text-secondary). Add tests for the filter, the threshold, the empty state and the keyboard (Enter, arrows, Escape twice). Fail-first for any new guard. model-menu-search · proposal
Model menu search · proposal
A search field for the composer's model menu, so a long provider list such as OpenRouter's stays usable. It reuses Field/Search, Menu/Popover, Menu/Section Title and Menu/Row; nothing new is added to the design system. Approved on 2026-10-20. Model names and counts are examples.
1. A long list opens with a search field
When the menu lists more than 12 models, a search field sits at its top and the menu opens with the cursor in it, so typing filters at once. The list scrolls under the field; the field stays put.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_ax_find
entries.description:
Search the accessibility elements captured by the last app_screenshot of one window. Filter by role (e.g. "AXTextArea", "AXButton") and/or title substring. Returns matching elements with their [N] index — pass that as element_index to app_click/app_type. Use this when the inline summary in app_screenshot doesn't show the element you need (it only lists the first few actionable ones).

This tool acts on one application in the BACKGROUND while the user keeps working in other apps. The target window does not come to the front. For the menu bar use app_menu; hover states and context menus still need the display-scope screenshot/left_click tools (which do take over the screen).

app.description: Bundle identifier of the target application (e.g. "com.apple.TextEdit"). Must be in the granted-applications list — call request_access first if it isn't.

window_id.description: CGWindowID from app_list_windows or from a previous app_screenshot result. If omitted, defaults to the window you most recently app_screenshot-ed for this app (or the app's main window if you haven't screenshotted yet). Pass a different id to switch windows — there is no separate switch-window tool; targeting is per-call via this parameter.

role.description: Exact AX role to match (e.g. "AXButton", "AXTextArea", "AXLink", "AXComboBox"). Omit to match any role.

title_contains.description: Case-insensitive substring to match against the element's title. Omit to match any title.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_batch
entries.description:
Execute a sequence of app_* actions against ONE window in a single tool call. Each individual app_* call is a model→API round trip; batching a predictable sequence (e.g. click a field, type into it, press return) eliminates all but one. Actions execute sequentially and stop on the first error or 'unsupported' result. An 'ineffective' result (write accepted, app didn't visibly respond yet) does NOT stop the batch — include a screenshot action after to verify. Typed text that comes back 'Not confirmed' DOES stop it. Include {"action":"screenshot"} anywhere in the list to capture the window at that point — coordinates and element_index in actions AFTER a screenshot refer to that screenshot. Put one last to see the post-batch state in the same call.

entries.description:

In a background Chromium or Electron app a click that goes out as raw input may carry the Command key on its press. The result says so when it did: most pages ignore it, but a list may toggle the item and an editor may add a cursor.

Press escape once; another with nothing left to cancel only plays the Mac's alert sound.

---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

---

description: "Render the built AgentUI/HomeUI bundles in the built-in browser with a scripted fake native host, to see page states the live app makes hard to catch"

Both pages find their host through `window.wx.postMessage(json)` and receive host
envelopes through `window.__jusprinBridge.deliver(envelope)` (`WebShared/bridgeClient.ts`).
Copy `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` to a scratch dir, inject
`<script>` right after `<head>` that (1) defines `window.wx` answering `hello` with
`hello_ack` + a full `state`, and (2) exposes `window.fake.deliver(type, payload)`;
serve with `python3 -m http.server` and open `agent.html?panel=printer` /
`home.html` via `preview_start`. Drive it with `javascript_tool`: deliver
`assistant_started` with no `assistant_delta` to freeze a streaming empty turn,
`printer_session` to pin a card, `printer_added` for Home's receipt strip. A file
drop works with `new DragEvent('drop', {dataTransfer})` on `.app--printer`.
Envelope: `{protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge'|'jusprin-home-bridge', version:1, id, type, payload}`.
Used 2026-09-19 to review branch these-commits-are-probably-wrong in ~10 minutes.

**Why:** the desktop tools were locked by another session and background
`app_click` never reaches WKWebView content, so page-level states (streaming
activity line, compact photo chip, leave dialog, receipt strip) had no other cheap
proof. It proves page rendering only; host behaviour (e.g. the 256 KiB image
preview cap `kInlineImagePreviewCap` in `AgentHost.cpp`) must be replicated in
the fake by hand or checked live.

**How to apply:** reach for this before building a full app + datadir copy when the
question is "what does the page draw for state X". Pair with [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]]
for the host side. Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

content.content: 138:- Agent message box: one box with the `medium` radius, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` inside stroke, and `component.composer` insets (8 DIP padding, 4 DIP between staged files, the field, and the toolbar). input.message:
Both are built on claude/composer-redesign, uncommitted. Kenneth has the pictures.

A. Narrow pane. Composer measures the toolbar with every label at full length (a measuring class shows "Thinking:" and stops the shrinking), using a ResizeObserver, not a breakpoint. When the labels don't fit, it adds .composer-choices--narrow, which hides "Thinking:". Only the model picker can shrink, so its name gets the ellipsis after that. + and Send keep their size. The accessible name and the native title stay "Thinking: Medium" / "Model: Claude Opus 5.5". input.content:
---
name: webkit-click-does-not-focus-buttons
description: In the app's WKWebView a click never focuses a button, so a menu that closes on blur loses clicks on every row but the focused one; jsdom and Chromium tests hide it. Fixed 2026-10-20 in ActionMenu; repro recipe.
metadata:
  type: project
---

On macOS WebKit (the app's web view) a mouse press on a `<button>` does not focus it;
it blurs whatever had the focus to `<body>` with `relatedTarget` null. `ActionMenu`
focuses the current row on open and closes on a blur that leaves it, so before
2026-10-20 a click on any OTHER row closed the menu on mouse-down and the click
never arrived. Kenneth hit it as "clicking an Anthropic model to switch from an
OpenAI model does nothing"; it also broke other thinking levels, + menu items after
the first, and Delete in the chat's ⋯ menu (the blur rule dates from 8334b3395b,
2026-09-23). Fix (claude/composer-redesign, uncommitted at the time):
`onMouseDown={e => e.preventDefault()}` on `.chat-menu-list`, guarded by
ActionMenu.test.tsx ("keeps the focus where it is when a row is pressed").

**Why:** vitest (jsdom), userEvent and Playwright/Chromium all focus a clicked
button, so every test passed while the app was broken. The host test for the same
switch passed too.

**How to apply:** for any web control that closes on blur or depends on focus after
a click, test the press in real WebKit. Recipe: a ~60-line Swift program with an
NSWindow + WKWebView, focus element A from script, then `NSApp.sendEvent` a
leftMouseDown/Up NSEvent at element B and read a log back with
`evaluateJavaScript` (`swiftc -O repro.swift -o repro && ./repro`, no permissions
needed). The live app was unreachable that day: its window was on a Space
`app_bring_to_current_space` refused to move. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[composer-model-pickers]].

content.content:
Redesign the Agent composer, with native file picking and per-chat models

The message box at the bottom of the Agent pane now works like the input
box in ChatGPT and Claude, following the Composer proposal on the
"JusPrin v2" canvas.

Composer
- One bordered box holds staged attachments, the text field and a
  toolbar. The field grows a line at a time up to component.composer
  maxLines (8), then scrolls; the toolbar stays.
- + (32 DIP icon button) opens an upward menu: Photo or image, 3D model,
  G-code, Document (PDF). Send and Stop are 28 DIP, from new button
  recipes primarySmall and secondarySmall.
- While the field has focus the whole box carries the 2 DIP border-focus
  ring, from new --focus-width/--focus-offset variables.

Native file picker
- Each + choice sends pick_attachment {kind}. The host asks an injected
  picker (AgentWebView: a wxFileDialog, opened via CallAfter, never inside
  the web view's message handler) filtered to the extensions
  classify_attachment() files under that kind, and stages each chosen file
  through the same checks a page-read file gets (store_file_attachment).
  Advertised as native_file_picker; the browser file input remains only
  for pages outside the app.

Per-chat provider, model and thinking level
- Model and thinking pickers sit after +. The model menu lists each
  set-up provider's models (grouped under the provider's name when there
  is more than one) and ends with "Set up another provider…"; the thinking
  menu lists only the chosen model's levels and is left out when it has
  none. Switching model keeps the level if the new model has it.
- A chat's choice is stored with it (chatModel in the project's Agent
  document; absent means the default provider's default model) and
  applies from its next turn. The host builds an agent for the choice
  before a turn; an agent handed to the host (by its owner or by setup)
  counts as the default choice's, so a chat that never picked keeps it.
  Earlier turns replay provider-neutrally, so a switch needs no
  translation of the history.
- Model lists come from each provider (ModelCatalog/ModelCatalogFetch):
  Anthropic's GET /v1/models capabilities give effort levels (offered only
  with adaptive thinking); OpenRouter's /api/v1/models, filtered to models
  that take tools, gives reasoning efforts and defaults; OpenAI's
  /v1/models has no capability data, so text models are kept by name and
  GPT-5 and later and the o-series are offered low/medium/high.
- The level is sent as reasoning.effort (OpenAI, OpenRouter) or as
  output_config.effort with adaptive thinking (Anthropic); title requests
  never carry it.
- Protocol: set_chat_model, model_catalog, chat_model; capability
  model_choice. Setup already kept one key per provider; its footnote now
  says the model can be switched in any chat. The printer panel's photo
  composer has no pickers.

Tests: host tests for the picker and model choice (switching, fallback
when a key is gone, a provider that cannot be built, the installed agent
kept), model-list parsing for all three providers, per-chat storage,
request bodies with and without a level; page tests for the composer, the
pickers and the store; stylesheet guards for each new recipe, shown to
fail without it. A hidden live case, agent_live_tests "[models][live]",
passed against OpenAI on 2026-10-20 (list, gpt-5.4-nano at low, then
gpt-5.4-mini); Anthropic and OpenRouter are untested live. The review
page now applies the stylesheet's own :focus-visible rules to its focus
mark, so focus draws there as it does in the app.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M5D4QYAQ1SRYW0Q1JSRC6BWE

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
